title: ue says /oo/
parentNote: Today's team is ue, and it says oo, as in blue. The commonest slip is saying the letter's own name — "b-you" for blue — and it is an honest mistake, because ue really does say yoo in a few words further down the road. For now, oo is the one to practise: push your lips forward into a small circle, like blowing a bubble, and hold it steady. The other slip is sounding out both letters, so glue comes out "gloo-eh"; point at the ue as one chunk, exactly the way you did with ie and oe. Only a handful of words use this spelling — blue, glue, true, clue — so today is short on new words and long on practice. If your child is still going strong at the end, read the story a second time and let them do more of it.

activities.mouthCue: Push your lips forward into a tiny circle, like blowing a bubble, and hold it: ooo.
activities.prompt: Another team of two letters. They do not say u and then e. Together they say oo.
Two of these work on their own. One is a team of two letters saying one sound.
Three teams, three different sounds. Find the one that says oo.
Only two sounds in this word. The ue is one of them.
Same ending. Only the blend at the front has changed.
Three sounds this time: g, then l, then the team.
Keep the ue in one piece in the middle and add the s at the end.
Same ending. Only the first sound is different.
Listen right to the end. Is there an s on it?
All three start with tr. The sound after it decides which one you heard.

activities.title: The blue glue
activities.prompt: Read the story one line at a time. Tap any word you want to hear again.
lines: Sue made a kite with a stick, a rag and blue glue.
The glue got on the desk and on the dog.
Then Meg came in and sat on the desk.
Meg is stuck! Sue did tug and tug.
Meg got up, but the hat did not. It is still stuck.
It is true: the dog is blue and the desk is blue.
The kite is not blue. The kite is red!
